newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African debt cases rise in third quarter.
newsitem.headline: S.African debt cases rise in third quarter.

text.p: The total number of South African civil summonses and civil judgements rose a seasonally adjusted 3.7 and 0.3 percent quarter-on-quarter in the third quarter of 1996, the Central Statistical Service (CSS) said.

It said in a statement on Thursday that the increase in civil summonses for debt was mainly due to a 10.5 percent rise in goods sold on open account, followed by a 2.8 percent increase in professional and a 4.3 percent rise in non-professional services.

The largest contributors to the increase in civil judgements for debt were goods sold on open account -- up 10.8 percent -- followed by an 18.2 percent rise in money lent and 19.8 percent growth in and promissory notes, the CSS said.
